Company description: TopView S.r.l. is an Innovative UAS Engineering SME founded in 2013. Initially focused on the development and implementation of proprietary drones, today the company adopts a broader strategy, mainly engaging in activities for the integration of drones into business processes. The core business is made up of three macro-areas:
1.Specialized flight operations. Optical and thermographic inspections, and aerial photogrammetry, as well as experimental operations in complex scenarios;
2.Design and implementation of Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS); TopView designs and prototypes both UAS and payloads with specific sensors;
3.U-space and digital aviation: digital products and services for drones integration in the VLL airspace.
Over the years, the company's activity has involved the design and implementation of complex systems, such as payloads and sensors for drones in different application niches, integrating them with customized IoT sensors. This led to present PV-Watch (the first inspection service of photovoltaic systems with drones) at the Solar Expo in Milan in 2014. In the same year, the company received authorization for UAS flight operations by the Italian Civil Aviation Authority (ENAC) for experimental activities.
In 2015 The Company received its first Horizon 2020 Grant with EASY-PV project, aimed at reducing the costs of solar power plants inspections. Since then, TopView has been involved in many R&D projects by various organizations.
In 2016, together with a few other Italian companies (Leonardo, ENAV, IDS, EuroUSC Italia) The Company participated in the definition of U-space, the set of services aimed at regulating the safe and efficient access of drones in European airspace. With the European projects, the research activity has been consolidated and has been recognized by key players in the aerospace sector, including SESAR JU, Eurocontrol and Leonardo. Over the years, TopView has gained specific expertise on EGNSS downstream applications and U-space domain, participating in many projects as Partner or Coordinator with the project CERTIFLIGHT EUSPA (2022-ongoing). The project proposes to use the Galileo OSNMA function to certify the flight tracks of drones and ultralight aircraft within VLL airspace, developing a first prototype of U-space Legal Recording service;
In many of these projects, TopView has contributed to develop services and prototypes, also leading the related field testing and validation campaigns.In 2020, despite the effects of the pandemic, the company consolidated its mission with new research projects and consulting services, and with an important strategic collaboration agreement with Telespazio and D-flight (ENAV). Thanks to these R&D efforts and the know-how acquired, in 2021 TopView was the first company to concretely adhere to the "U-space Manifesto" launched by D-Flight, the Italian provider of unmanned air traffic management services. In fact, it has released a first version of Pollicino ™, the proprietary drone tracker that allows drones to interface with the U-space services of the national provider, promoting situational awareness and safety of operations in VLL (Very Low Level) airspace. Internal R&D activities also include Urban Air Mobility, with a patented concpet of a drone taxi for the transport of passengers.

SCOR, the world’s fourth largest reinsurer, offers its clients a diversified and innovative range of solutions and services to control and manage risk. 

The Group generated premiums of more than EUR 16 billion in 2019, and serves clients in more than 160 countries from its 38 offices worldwide, with around 2,900 employees.

SCOR Europe SE, a 100%-owned subsidiary of SCOR SE, is a Paris-based P&C specialty insurance company, which has been approved by the French supervisory authority, the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution). This license enables SCOR Europe SE to operate within the European Economic Area (EEA) with effect from January 1, 2019 and enables the Group to ensure the continuity of the services offered to its insured clients in view of Brexit. With effect from January 1, 2019, SCOR Europe SE underwrites all new and renewed business relating to risks located in the EEA. SCOR Europe SE has no staff under contract but benefits from the support of SCOR SE employees.

SCOR Europe SE benefits from the SCOR group’s financial strength, which is recognized by the rating agencies. S&P in particular has assigned SCOR Europe SE an AA- rating.

entityDescription: Europe's Spaceport is situated in the northeast of South America in French Guiana, an overseas department of France. In 1964 the French Government chose Kourou, from 14 other sites, as a base from which to launch its satellites. When the European Space Agency came into being in 1975, the French Government offered to share its Centre Spatial Guyanais (CSG) with ESA. For its part, ESA approved funding to upgrade the launch facilities at the CSG to prepare the Spaceport for the Ariane launchers under development. Since then, ESA has continued to fund two thirds of the spaceport's annual budget to finance the operations and the investments needed to maintain the top level services provided by the Spaceport. ESA also finances new facilities, such as launch complexes and industrial production facilities, for new launchers such as Vega-C and Ariane 6.

Université d’Évry-Val-d’Essonne is a higher education establishment, part of Université Paris-Saclay, which gathers 15% of France research.
Université d’Évry-Val-d’Essonne cutting-edge research’s strength concerns Genomics and post-genomics for precision medicine and genome-related industry (innovative biotherapies, synthetic biology…), Applied mathematics for finance and genomics, Information and communication technology (ICT), as well as research in Robotics and for Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) or Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV), and Space technology. Université d’Évry-Val-d’Essonne extends its research with applications in close partnerships with two main R&D Clusters: Genopole the first French biocluster dedicated to innovative biotechnologies (see https://join-the-biocluster.genopole.fr/A-Business-Accelerator.html) and the Cluster “Drones Paris-Region” dedicated to UAS (see http://www.clusterdronesparisregion.com/), and in the framework of the French government program Careers and Qualifications Campus – Aeronautics and Space, currently under development where Université d’Évry-Val-d’Essonne is the leader.
Humanities and Social Sciences encompasses Economics, Law, Sociology and History. where research focus on market balance, compared public and private law, sociology of work, visual sociology and arts and music.
Finally, Université d’Évry-Val-d’Essonne’s campus life is vibrant and multicultural. Seminars, exhibitions, arts and cultural activities, sports: everything is in place to foster a dynamic campus at the heart of the Évry community. entityDescription:
Heraklion is the capital of Crete and one of the Mediterranean region's most fascinating and vibrant cities. The Chandax of the Arabs and Byzantines, the Candia of the Venetians, was one of the island's major ports and markets, and at times one of the most economically active towns in the wider region. Heraklion is the fourth largest city in Greece. According to the results of the 2011 census, the municipality's population is 173,993 people and it extends over an area of 684.3 km2 (264.2 sq mi).
The Municipality of Heraklion employs 751 workers. Heraklion has been selected as one of the Smart21 Communities of 2012, 2013 and 2014 by the Intelligent Community Forum and has been awarded European distinction and the second European Prize in the Dosta!-Congress Prize as recognition of the excellent efforts and its municipal program for the implementation of its social services pertaining to social inclusion and anti-discrimination. Furthermore Heraklion nominated Best City Destination and Gold Award Winner in Greek Travel Awards in Stockholm, was also one of the Winner for UNESCO Learning Cities Award of the 2019, with its ‘Fit for All’ programme, through which Heraklion has found an innovative and fun way to bring its citizens and the refugees residing in the city closer together by promoting equity and inclusion through sports and educational activities based on subjects such as local culture and tradition.

Intelligent Environments S.L. (IE) is a company with 100% Spanish capital, specialized in software and data quality evaluation and improvement, which was created in 2006 as a university spinoff. IE is composed of highly qualified professionals (Engineers and PhDs in Computer Science) with experience in software and data quality, software development and maintenance methodologies, process and project management, governance and auditing, and business engineering. 

The company is committed to innovation, with continuous interaction with the university environment, as we consider research and innovation to be essential elements for the improvement and sustainability of information systems, having participated in more than 10 R+D+i projects in recent years.

IE specializes in measuring, evaluating and improving the quality of software and data. As a result of this, AQCLab was created in 2010 as the first and only laboratory at an international level that is accredited by ENAC (National Accreditation Entity) and ILAC for the evaluation of software product and data quality, following the good practices of the international standard ISO/IEC 25000.

Thanks to AQCLab's assessments, organizations can not only evaluate and improve the quality of their software and data, but also obtain a quality certification in ISO/IEC 25000, issued by a certification body such as AENOR.

entityDescription:
ENGIE Impact Belgium S.A. is a spin-off of the “Advisory & Advanced Analytics” department (previously known as the “Energy Transition” department) of Tractebel Engineering S.A..
ENGIE Impact accelerates sustainability transformation for corporations, cities and governments. We help organizations embed sustainability into their operational strategies, allowing them to bridge the gap between sustainability commitments and realized results that capture economic value and make organizations more competitive over the long term. ENGIE Impact applies data analytics, multi-disciplinary expertise and global reach to accelerate sustainability transformation of organizations around the world. The process starts with tailored roadmaps to help organizations establish and achieve their sustainability goals. This guidance is grounded in reliable data and advanced analytics, creating a holistic view across resources: energy, water, waste and carbon. From strategy to implementation, actionable solutions help clients improve their bottom line, drive growth, satisfy stakeholders and extend resources. ENGIE Impact is currently working with more than 1,000 Corporations, Cities, Governments managing more than 1,000,000 sites around the world. Our more than 2,000 employees are spread in 13 locations worldwide. Sustainability Solutions (Europe Middle East Africa India – EMEAI) ENGIE Impact Sustainability Solutions department gives our customers the support needed with regulatory, financial, economic, technical, engineering and digital matters. ENGIE Impact has the key expertise & references to propose a holistic and systemic approach to address the energy transition needs. This includes all interactions between the energy system’s components and stakeholders over the entire value chain. Advisory services of ENGIE Impact covers policies and regulatory aspects, macro-economics and market design/analyses, energy system consulting (power, gas, district heating/cooling, CO2, energy access), smart decentralized solutions, smart cities (telecom, mobility and energy interactions), renewable energy sources, energy efficiency (data centers, industrial, commercial and residential buildings) and energy storage systems (hydrogen, thermal, battery, etc). Strongly connected with our advisory services, our Sustainability Solutions team offers also Advanced Analytics services englobing Simulation, Optimisation and Data Analytics (Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Big Data, IoT). Depending on the needs, we can either develop commercial software or tailor-made applications, used by our customers. Advanced Analytics aspects especially focus on economic optimization, aiming at providing a direct impact on clients financial bottom line. Example of application fields includes Predictive maintenance (Wind, Solar, Hydro Power Generation, Industry,...), District Heating and Cooling Networks, Power Transportation and Distribution Networks, Multifluid Smart Grid Optimization, Shipping Fleet Optimization, Hydropower optimization, Gas storage, Energy Trading, Smart home connected services,... Our international experts’ network can take advantage of shared knowledge worldwide while bringing in local expertise from our regional offices to assist you on each of your projects.

entityName: TECHNISCHE UNIVERSITAT DRESDEN - Chair for Circuit Design and Network Theory
entityDescription:
The Chair for Circuit Design and Network Theory is dedicated to the design and modeling of integrated circuits in CMOS, BiCMOS and III/V technologies, as well as emerging "beyond moore" nano-technologies, e.g. those based on carbon nanotubes, silicon nanowires and organic as well as polymeric devices.
The focus is on analysis and design of analog and mixed-signal circuits. Other areas of work include the design of FPGA, PCBs and hybrid assemblies, digital signal processing and algorithms for complete information systems. Applications include high-frequency systems, wireless communication from low-frequency-range up to 220 GHz, optical data transmission up to 80 Gbit/s, high-precision positioning systems, energy-adaptive systems with intelligent, dynamic control and wake-up features as well as energy harvesting. In addition, the professorship has experience in the development and optimization of high-end audio systems and speakers.

entityDescription: Port of Tallinn is the biggest port authority in Estonia and its strategic goal is to develop the competitiveness of Estonia as a maritime country. Its harbours are navigable and easily accessible through the year and deep enough to receive all vessels passing through the Danish Straits. Estonia’s geographical location is favourable for handling both north-south and east-west passenger and cargo flows. Tallinna Sadam owns two passenger harbours (the Old City Harbour and the Saaremaa Harbour) and two cargo harbours (the Muuga Harbour and the Paldiski South Harbour). In terms of the number of passengers served, Tallinn Old City Harbour is the third-largest harbour on the Baltic Sea (after Helsinki and Stockholm) and the fourth-largest in Northern Europe. The Muuga Harbour is Estonia’s largest cargo harbour. Tallinna Sadam offers port services as a landlord port, i.e. it owns, administers and develops berths and port basins, leases land to cargo operators, organises vessel traffic in port basins and ensures safe navigation in port waters. Tallinna Sadam owns passenger terminals and other facilities required for passenger service but cargo harbour superstructure belongs to cargo operators. Waste management service in harbours is provided by AS Green Marine, an associate of Tallinna Sadam that offers innovative waste handling solutions.
